Operation
ŏp-er-ā´shun
n. (working, active power; rendering Hebrew maaseh, Greek energeia)
From Latin operari, to work. An operation is God's working — the Greek gives us energy.

Biblical Definition

An operation is a working. Isaiah pronounces woe on those who “regard not the work of the LORD, neither consider the operation of his hands” (Isa 5:12). Paul distinguishes gifts, administrations, and operations: “there are diversities of operations, but it is the same God which worketh all in all” (1Co 12:6). Colossians says believers are risen with Christ “through the faith of the operation of God, who hath raised him from the dead” (Col 2:12).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines operation as the act or process of operating; agency; the exertion of power, physical, mechanical or moral; and action, effect.

expand to see more

OPERATION, n. The act or process of operating; agency; the exertion of power, physical, mechanical or moral.

2. Action; effect.

3. Process; manipulation; series of acts in experiments.

4. In surgery, any methodical action of the hand on the human body.

Key Scripture

Isa 5:12 — "And the harp, and the viol, the tabret, and pipe, and wine, are in their feasts: but they regard not the work of the LORD, neither consider the operation of his hands."

1Co 12:6 — "And there are diversities of operations, but it is the same God which worketh all in all."

Col 2:12 — "Buried with him in baptism, wherein also ye are risen with him through the faith of the operation of God, who hath raised him from the dead."

Psa 28:5 — "Because they regard not the works of the LORD, nor the operation of his hands, he shall destroy them, and not build them up."

Modern Corruption

God's activity is assumed to be visible only in the extraordinary, and Isaiah's woe falls on people too entertained to notice the operation of His hands.

expand to see more

Isaiah 5:12 lists what occupied them instead: the harp, and the viol, the tabret, and pipe, and wine, are in their feasts: but they regard not the work of the LORD, neither consider the operation of his hands. Nothing on the list is sinful. The charge is inattention — a life so continuously furnished with pleasant noise that the working of God passes unremarked. Psalm 28:5 attaches a consequence: because they regard not the works of the LORD… he shall destroy them, and not build them up.

1 Corinthians 12:6 is the reassuring counterpart for a congregation comparing itself: there are diversities of operations, but it is the same God which worketh all in all. The variety is real and it is deliberate; the source is single. Whatever a member is doing that is genuinely of God is God's own working, which makes both envy and contempt category errors.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew maaseh (H4639), a work or deed; Greek energeia (G1753), operative power; energema (G1755), an effect worked.

expand to see more

Hebrew maaseh (H4639) — work, operation; Isaiah 5:12, Psalm 28:5.

Greek energema (G1755) — operation, effect; 1 Corinthians 12:6, 10.

Greek energeia (G1753) — working, energy; Colossians 2:12, Ephesians 1:19, 3:7.

Usage

"“Neither consider the operation of his hands” — woe pronounced on inattention."

"“Diversities of operations, but it is the same God” — variety with one source."

"“Through the faith of the operation of God” — resurrection power applied."
